predecessors.name: Beylik of Hamid (Hamidids)
predecessors.text: Antalya and the Teke Peninsula, the part of the Hamidid lands held by the Teke branch

predecessors.name: Sultanate of Rum
predecessors.text: the Teke lands, formerly Seljuk (Antalya taken by the Seljuks in 1207)

ledger.x: 1321: a Hamidid branch founds the Teke beylik at Antalya.
August 1361: Peter I of Cyprus takes Antalya.
1391: Bayezid I annexes the Teke beylik.
1423: the Ottomans annex Teke for good.

wars.name: Cypriot conquest of Antalya
wars.outcome: Peter I conquered Antalya on 24 August 1361; the emir of Antalya, Teke, 'after many attacks tried to occupy his city' but failed; Cypriot rule lasted until 1373.

wars.name: Ottoman annexation of Teke
wars.outcome: Bayezid I annexed the beylik in 1391; Timur restored Othman in 1402; the Ottomans annexed it again in 1423.

wars.name: Battle of Ankara
wars.outcome: 'In the fateful Battle of Ankara, on 20 July 1402, the Ottoman army was defeated'; Timur restored the beys, among them Othman of Teke.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Taurus and Lycian highland frontiers with Karaman, Hamid, Germiyan and Menteshe are approximate.
